sam_sales: Hey team — Nebula (enterprise POC) wants Redwood Private. Their compliance requires BYOK with HSM attestation + client TLS certs. They also asked for a short timeline and whether we can avoid sending any plaintext keys.
patrick_se: +1. We should do an HSM-backed BYOK flow. We support: AWS CloudHSM (import tokens), PKCS#11 HSMs, and KMS import for wrapped keys. They can either: 1) give us a public wrapping key (RSA/OAEP) and we wrap keys, or 2) import wrapped key material into their HSM and give us a reference.
patrick_se: For the POC I'd recommend the public-wrapping-key flow — fastest. Also need mutual TLS between their VPC and our private control plane for cert-based API auth.
maria_infra: Quick ops notes: we'll need their VPC CIDR + peering details (or Transit GW), and an allowed inbound SG for our control plane IPs. For the certs we can do a CSR from our side or accept a client cert from them. Which do they prefer?
sam_sales: They prefer us to generate the key material and provide a CSR for mTLS client certs so they can sign with their internal CA. They explicitly said no plaintext private keys crossing networks.
patrick_se: Perfect — workflow: 1) Redwood generates CSR + ephemeral RSA key on our infra (private key never leaves enclave). 2) We send CSR to Nebula. 3) Nebula returns CA-signed client cert. 4) We pin the cert and enable mTLS on the private control plane. For BYOK: they provide an RSA public-wrapping-key in PEM (PKCS#1) and HSM attestation (if available).
patrick_se: Example commands for their ops team to generate a wrapping key and export public part:
```
# on their HSM or openssl if they just share pubkey
openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:4096 -out private_wrap.pem
openssl rsa -in private_wrap.pem -pubout -out wrapping_pub.pem
```
If it's a PKCS#11 HSM, they can export the public key via pkcs11-tool and give us wrapping_pub.pem.
oliver_security: Security checklist to include in the SOW (short):
- Delivery method: signed S3 URL with TLS + enforced ACLs OR SFTP with key auth
- No plaintext private keys permitted in any transfer
- HSM attestation report or vendor-signed quote (optional but preferred)
- Client cert must include OU=nebula-poc and expire within 90 days for POC
- Audit log retention for all key operations during POC
Please send them a checklist doc; I'll review.
sam_sales: I'll send an initial email today. Can you draft the checklist + a one-page POC steps doc (ops-friendly) so I can attach?
maria_infra: I can draft the ops checklist. Timeline estimate: network peering + routing rules: 24-48h (once we have VPC info). CSR + signing: 1 business day (depends on Nebula CA). Dedicated pool + config for private: ~48h queue. So overall ~3-5 business days if no approvals block.
patrick_se: Also flag pricing: Private POC uses a small reserved pool for stability; we typically quote a 2-week dev POC rate with metered overage. Sam — check Sales quoting template for 'private-poc-2wk' SKU.
sam_sales: noted, I'll attach preliminary quote. One more: client asked whether we can do HSM import directly into their CloudHSM and have Redwood call it. Answer?
patrick_se: We don't hold customers' HSMs. Options: a) they keep keys in their HSM and we use a PKCS#11 proxy in their VPC to perform signing operations (requires private deployment + connector), or b) they provide wrapped symmetric keys that we unwrap using their public wrapping key and store encrypted in our secure enclave. For a POC, b) is simpler. For PROD, option (a) is preferred for full separation.
oliver_security: Add to checklist: if using PKCS#11 proxy, we need customer to run the signing agent in their VPC and provide endpoint + auth token. We'll require mTLS and IAM rules.
sam_sales: Great. Patrick/Maria — can you put the ops snippet + packing list into a Gdoc and share with me by EOD? I'll loop Nebula.
patrick_se: On it. I'll drop an initial doc link here when ready.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created doc "nebula-private-poc-onboarding-draft" (link: https://redwood.internal/docs/nebula-private-poc-onboarding-draft)
patrick_se: Link has the CSR template, wrapping key spec, example commands, and the S3 + SFTP options. Please review before I send.
sam_sales: thanks — will review and send to Nebula. Tagging @oliver_security if they have any final redlines. :thumbsup:
oliver_security: minor nit: require signed metadata file (.json) accompanying any PEM with SHA256 checksums. Other than that looks good.
sam_sales: copying that into the doc and sending now. Will update thread with client responses.
